result.process_description:
The Evanstonian is an upscale independent hotel.
When a guest calls room service at The Evanstonian, the room-service manager takes down the order.
She then submits an order ticket to the kitchen to begin preparing the food.
She also gives an order to the sommelier (i.e., the wine waiter) to fetch wine from the cellar and to prepare any other alcoholic beverages.
Eighty percent of room-service orders include wine or some other alcoholic beverage.
Finally, she assigns the order to the waiter.
While the kitchen and the sommelier are doing their tasks, the waiter readies a cart (i.e., puts a tablecloth on the cart and gathers silverware).
The waiter is also responsible for nonalcoholic drinks.
Once the food, wine, and cart are ready, the waiter delivers it to the guest's room.
After returning to the room-service station, the waiter debits the guest's account.
The waiter may wait to do the billing if he has another order to prepare or deliver.

result.rule: Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant performs a concrete preparatory action (for example, readying or gathering items) while other parallel work is happening, so the action runs alongside those branches rather than being part of them: Model each such stated action as its own bpmn:task inside the branch of the parallel gateway that runs alongside the other work, and join that branch at the parallel gateway that waits for all work to finish. Do not omit the action or fold it into a neighbouring task.

When the description states that one step is followed by several actions that the same actor performs without a stated order, and all of them must be carried out before the process moves on: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one branch per stated action, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not connect the actions in a sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway, because all branches must complete.

When the description states that an actor may postpone a stated action (for example, waiting before doing it) when another pending obligation of that same actor exists, so the postponement depends on that circumstance: Model the postponement as an exclusive gateway placed before the postponed action. One conditional outgoing flow leads to the postponed action as its own bpmn:task, with the stated circumstance as its condition. The other flow leads to the other pending obligation. Join the branches again after the postponed action so that the postponed action is kept as a separate task, not dropped or merged into a neighbouring task.

When the description states that two or more activities are performed independently, by different teams or systems, and a later step can proceed only after all of them have finished: Model a parallel gateway that forks the flow before the independent activities and a parallel gateway that joins them before the first step that needs all of them, instead of a sequential chain or an exclusive gateway.
